purpose: Measure whether existing frozen Lean FPN features distinguish annotated polyp from overextended predicted foreground when contrasted against the first automatic prompt's own features.
frames: The first automatically detected frame and four fixed, equally spaced manifest indices from that first frame to the last frame, rounded to the nearest integer and deduplicated; no annotation drives selection. Sequence 3 is an engineering replay only.
inference: Replay the audited indexed-position Lean reference exactly with identical automatic first box, feature points, mask and memory routing. Observe the existing backbone FPN features at the selected frames. At the first automatic prompt use the saved automatic initial mask (never GT) with the existing reference_prototypes routine to produce foreground and background mean descriptors for each FPN level. For each selected frame save positive-cosine and positive-minus-background-cosine maps; do not change model inference. Require all video masks, token selection and position receipts to match the audited indexed reference exactly.
analysis: Only after inference, use label images for soft area-weighted ROC AUC of each score over whole images and separately within the reference predicted foreground; compare positive-only versus positive-minus-background rankings at each FPN level. Empty-label frames have undefined AUC. No classification threshold, re-detection, ground-truth inference, adaptive gating or claim of video improvement. Do not fit a method to these previously inspected exploratory cases.
validation: Source-replay engineering checks and unit tests for the weighted AUC implementation and empty-label handling. Two independent label-free seq3 runs must exactly match indexed reference masks, selections and positions and reproduce maps and source hashes before the selected videos.
limitations: Small, retrospectively selected sequences; first automatic prompt can be incorrect or on a labeled-empty frame. Pixel-cell ROC AUC ignores temporal propagation and may overstate performance; labels may be incomplete and frames are not independent. This is a diagnostic, not proof that contrast improves segmentation.
